newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil firm with crude, strike, tightness.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil firm with crude, strike, tightness.

text.p: NWE fuel oil was stronger on Thursday buoyed by crude, the refinery strike at Elf and tightness in some sectors.
Dealers said high sulphur barges regained Wednesday's losses with trades done as high $126 fob ARA. A cargo was sold to a U.K utility on a 50:50 basis of $123 cif NWE and cif mean.
"High sulphur is stable, but its strength is coming more from crude rather than increased tightness or supply," said one trader.

The Elf strike, now in its eighth day, has meant the group has lost approximately 80,000 tonnes of fuel oil production and there has been rising speculation that force majeure would have to be declared.

"It would not be unreasonable to declare force majeure, I would if I was them," said a trader at a major. Elf has not been actively buying material, picking up only a bunker spec cargo in the Med from Italy.
Low sulphur cracked fuel has strength aside from crude with deals done yesterday at $140 fob Med and $136 fob NWE.
